project_name: Number Portability Administration Center Service Management System
initial_requirements: Telecommunications service providers need a shared administration system for moving customers' telephone numbers between provider networks. The system should receive information from the old and new providers, validate and coordinate their requests, activate agreed routing changes, and distribute updated portability data to participating networks. Operations personnel also need transaction history, conflict handling, reporting, and audit capabilities to keep provider records synchronized.

messages.content: What are the primary business goals and success criteria for this shared number portability administration system—for example, which outcomes matter most around turnaround time, accuracy, regulatory compliance, and reducing coordination effort between providers?

The main business goal is to make number porting faster and more reliable while keeping all providers synchronized on the same source of truth. We want requests validated quickly, routing changes activated on time, and very few errors or manual reconciliations, because delays and mismatches directly affect customer service.
Success would mean short turnaround from request submission to completion, high accuracy in matching and updating portability data, and full compliance with regulatory and audit requirements. It also matters a lot that the system reduces back-and-forth between providers, so operations teams spend less time coordinating exceptions and more time handling only the true conflicts or exceptions.
Which stakeholder roles or user groups will interact with this number portability administration system, and what responsibilities or permissions should each role have?

The main users would be operations staff from the participating telecom providers, plus a central administration or NPAC-style operations team that oversees the process. Provider users would submit and receive porting data, check request status, respond to conflicts, and correct records for their own company, while the central team would validate transactions, manage exceptions, trigger routing updates, and monitor the shared data set. We’d also expect read-only access for auditors or compliance users, since they need history and traceability but shouldn’t be changing transactions.

Can you walk me through the full number-porting lifecycle the system needs to support—from initial submission through validation, conflict handling, approval, routing activation, and final completion—and highlight any timing or validation rules that must be enforced at each step?

A port would start when the gaining provider submits the request and the losing provider’s information is captured into the shared system. Then the system should validate the request details, check that the number is eligible, and make sure the records from both providers line up before anything is activated. If there’s a mismatch or a dispute, it needs to pause in a conflict state until the providers resolve it or the operations team intervenes.
Once the request is approved, the system should schedule or trigger the routing update and distribute the new portability data to all participating networks as quickly as required by the process. After activation, the transaction should close out as completed, with a full audit trail showing who submitted, who approved, what changed, and when each step happened. I don’t know the exact timing windows offhand, because those usually depend on the regulatory rules and operational agreements, but the system definitely needs to enforce whatever cutoffs and completion deadlines those rules require.

Since the exact timing windows, cutoffs, and completion deadlines depend on regulatory rules and operational agreements, how should the system store, configure, and apply those timing rules—by jurisdiction, regulator, provider group, or another basis—and what kinds of changes or exceptions should authorized users be able to manage without code changes?

I’d expect those timing rules to be configured centrally as data, not hardcoded, with the ability to vary by jurisdiction and regulator first, and then by provider group or process type if needed. The system should be able to apply the right rule set based on the port’s context, so one transaction can follow a different deadline than another without custom development. Authorized users should be able to update cutoffs, business days, holidays, SLA windows, and exception handling rules through administration screens, but not change the core validation logic itself.

When a porting request is approaching a deadline, enters a conflict state, or requires escalation, who should be notified and through which channels should those notifications be delivered (for example, in-app alerts, email, SMS, or integration messages to provider systems)?

The gaining and losing provider operational contacts should be notified first, and the central operations team should also get alerted when a deadline is at risk or a conflict is created. In-app alerts are important for users working directly in the system, but email would be needed for broader visibility and after-hours follow-up. For urgent escalations, SMS or automated integration messages to provider systems would be useful, though I’d want to keep the exact channel mix configurable by severity and by provider preference.
